verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for after work (16:30 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: TODAY after work from about 16:30 at Rey Cortiço is the best available option, but I’m treating it as a cam-check first. The wind looks a bit unfriendly for that spot and Surfline’s been inconsistent, so I’d look at Surfline cams and the MEO Beachcam before you leave—if it doesn’t look much better than expected, don’t bother. If the sandbanks are lining up on the video and it’s not getting blown out, mid-rising tide should at least keep it workable.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Low confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 50 kJ, 10 s period, lully 27/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 10-13s at mid tide also works on Belgas, but low tide is not a deal-breaker, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
